analyses.spec_says: contract.json:849 (CHK-025 stimulus): "Drive i_wr_en=1 with new distinct data at every write edge from W0 until 10 write cycles after o_sw_rst_busy falls." contract.json:850 (expected 8): "The first post-reset word P0 is accepted at m+1. o_rd_data=P0 from the second read edge after it, while o_empty is still 1; o_empty falls only from read edge 3." This is the model-off number. Spec 10.3 (spec:517, rules.json AF-10.3-02 line 4992): "With the metastability model (REQ-VER-001) the flag changes after destination edge S, S+1, or S+2". This sentence has no 'isolated' qualifier. CHK-015 limits that window to isolated changes (contract.json:581): "each isolated pointer change becomes visible after destination edge S, S+1 or S+2". Spec 10.6.4 (spec:653, AF-10.6.4-01 rules.json:5481): "Each bit of the synchronized vector is independent... If the input changes again while a change is pending, the pending value is replaced by the new input value and the delay restarts." spec:685: "A pending change that is replaced (event 4) can make a short pulse disappear on the model output. This is intended".
analyses.rtl_does: The write side increments the pointer on every accepted write (m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:129-138; Gray at :138). The reads after P0 give: P0 at m+1 makes wbin 0->1 (Gray 0000->0001, bit0 rises). P1 at m+2 makes Gray 0011 (bit1 rises). P2 at m+3 makes Gray 0010 (bit0 falls). So at the source, bit0 is 1 for only 2 write cycles (20 ns), which is shorter than 2 read periods (28 ns). In the per-bit model (m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182), the bit0 rise is detected at the last-stage input (:158). If extra>=1 is chosen (:165-168), the fall of bit0 arrives one read edge later and replaces the pending rise (:158-160), so the bit0 rise never reaches o_q. The first change that w_wgray_s then shows is bit1. Bit1 launched one write cycle later, so its edge 1 can be P0's edge 2, and with extra=2 it appears after P0-relative edge S+3. o_empty = w_rd_blk | (reg_rgray == w_wgray_s) (m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:97,117), so it falls at S+3. That matches 'got 5' with S=2 and 'got 6' with S=3. No data error results: when bit1 appears first, the decoded pointer is 3 and P0..P2 are already written. The E2[1] o_rd_data==P0 check on the line before (test:1152) passed. This is consistent with the model being on: model_off/syn pass. wr_slow.s1 uses the same CHK-025 clocks and start delays as base.s1, which passes (both 3820/4664 ps). The only difference is the per-cell random stream state left by the earlier tests, so the result depends on the draw. I inferred this from the code and the L values; there is no waveform in the directory.
analyses.test_does: test:1098-1113 keeps i_wr_en=1 with new data at every write edge until fall+10, so P0, P1, P2... are written at consecutive write edges (10 ns write, 14 ns read, test:1070). test:1145-1150: P0 = Wr[m+1].i_wr_data, e2 = first read edge after write edge m+1, E2 = Rr[e2:e2+LMAX+2]. test:1153 runs chk_lat(lead(E2,'o_empty',1)). chk_lat (test:90-93) accepts S..LMAX with LMAX = S+EXTRA and EXTRA=2 when the model is on (test:46-49). The test docstring (test:12-13) states "exactly S with the metastability model off, S..S+2 with the model on (DEC-012)". So the window is the isolated-change window from CHK-015, applied to the first word of a back-to-back burst.

candidates.evidence_for: The test applies the isolated-change window S..S+2 (CHK-015, contract.json:581) to P0, but its own stimulus makes P0 non-isolated: P1 and P2 follow at the next write edges (test:1110-1112). Under the spec's model (spec:653, spec:685) the short bit0 pulse can be removed, so the first visible change comes from bit1, which was launched one write cycle later. That allows S+3 relative to P0. Model-off and syn runs pass the exact S check. The failure appears only with the model on and depends on the random draw (wr_slow.s1 fails, base.s1 with the same clocks and phases passes).
candidates.evidence_against: Contract CHK-025 (8) says 'o_empty falls only from read edge 3' and gives no extra allowance for the model. Spec 10.3 (spec:517) states S..S+2 with no 'isolated' condition, so the test author followed the literal spec text.

candidates.evidence_for: spec:517 / AF-10.3-02 give S..S+2 for 'a source pointer update' with no restriction. spec:653 and :685 define a per-bit model in which a pending change is replaced and 'a short pulse [can] disappear'. Together, these mean a pointer update followed by more updates within about 2 destination cycles can become visible later than S+2. The spec never states the bound for back-to-back updates. spec:684 ('a late bit makes the destination domain see the previous pointer value') also assumes isolated updates.
candidates.evidence_against: CHK-015 (contract.json:581-583) and TEST-008 (rules.json:8782) already limit the S..S+2 claim to isolated changes, so a careful reading gives the qualifier.

candidates.evidence_for: The removal of a short pulse comes from the simulation model inside the RTL file m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:158-169. A designer could decide the model should never swallow a Gray-pointer bit change that is followed by another bit's change.
candidates.evidence_against: The model does what spec:653 and spec:685 say ('This is intended'). The FIFO logic (rd.sv:97,117) is a plain compare. Exact latency S passes in model_off.s1 and syn.s1 and in all other model-on runs except two draws. No data or flag-safety error is reported (CHK-005/CHK-006 0 fails, results.json:977-1100).

analyses.options: (1) Fix the test: for (8), either make P0 isolated in the model-on runs (write P0 alone, then wait at least LMAX+1 read edges before P1), or measure o_empty's fall against the latest bound over the words written back-to-back. That is: o_empty must be 1 through edge S-1 (never early) and must fall by S+2 after P1's write edge, i.e. by S+3 relative to P0, with the bound derived from the spec. Keep the exact S check in model-off runs. This is a correct derivation for non-isolated stimulus, not a looser check. (2) Clarify the spec: add to 10.3/10.6.4 the latency bound when a pointer update is followed by another update within S+2 destination cycles (a swallowed pulse makes the first visible change come from the next update), and update CHK-025 (8) to match. (3) If the designer wants a removed pulse never to delay the first visible change, change the model in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:158-169. For example, do not let a new input value cancel a pending change of the opposite value before it is output. Then update spec:653/:685, which currently call the replacement intended.

analyses.failure: CHK-003 assertion: 534 fails / 1,523,017 hits. First fail 239,353,000 ps (base.s1), during test_chk_016_random_ratios/pair=2 (10 ns write / 23 ns read; base.s1.log:68-75). Fails are 0 in model_off.s1 and syn.s1 and non-zero in every model-on run (results.json:851-913).
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:287: "At every rising edge of i_clk_rd, and while i_rst_n_rd=0: (a) if o_empty=1, then o_empty_thr=1... (b) If i_empty_thr >= PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_empty_thr=1. (c) If i_empty_thr==0, then o_empty_thr == o_empty." Note the wording 'while i_rst_n_rd=0' is ambiguous: it probably means 'and also while'. REQ-FUNC-010 (spec:139): "o_empty_thr shall be 1 when the read-domain occupancy estimate is less than or equal to i_empty_thr... the empty side (it can be smaller)". rules.json:13573: "It differs from the true occupancy only by pointer updates still inside the synchronizer". Model, spec:653 (AF-10.6.4-01, rules.json:5481): "Each bit of the synchronized vector is independent... extra delay of 0, 1, or 2 destination cycles... the pending value is replaced by the new input value". spec:684: "A Gray pointer changes one bit per update, so a late bit makes the destination domain see the previous pointer value for a while".
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:104-112: w_wbin_s = gray2bin(w_wgray_s); w_occ = w_wbin_s - reg_rbin (4-bit modulo). :117-118: o_empty = w_rd_blk | (reg_rgray==w_wgray_s); o_empty_thr = w_rd_blk ? 1 : (w_occ <= i_empty_thr). By construction (a) and (c) cannot fail. o_empty=1 means blocked or equal pointers (w_occ=0), so o_empty_thr=1. For thr=0, w_occ<=0 holds exactly when the Gray values are equal, i.e. when o_empty=1. So the failing clause must be (b): i_empty_thr in 8..15 while w_occ in 9..15 and not blocked. That needs a decoded write pointer more than DEPTH ahead of, or behind, reg_rbin, which a coherent Gray sequence cannot produce. The per-bit model (m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:98-182; one independent cell per bit, m_vlsit_afifo_sync.sv:46-56) can produce it when the write pointer changes on consecutive fast write edges. Example: wbin 3->4->5 is Gray 0010->0110->0111. If the bit2 rise is delayed 2 cycles and the bit0 rise is not, w_wgray_s=0011 = bin 2. That pointer has moved backwards. With reg_rbin=3, w_occ=15, o_empty=0, o_empty_thr=0. The sequence and failing clause are inferred from the code. The log has no per-clause or value printout (nnc_chk_rd.sv:77).
analyses.test_does: Checker nnc_chk_rd.sv:73-77: assert at every posedge i_clk_rd, with no disable iff (reset included): (!o_empty||o_empty_thr) && (i_empty_thr<DEPTH||o_empty_thr) && (i_empty_thr!=0 || o_empty_thr==o_empty). Hits are counted at every edge (:78). Stimulus at the first fail: test_chk_016 pair (10,23) with random thresholds ft,et = r.randint(0,TMAX) (test:763-765), random traffic, and the model on. During reset the synchronizer and rbin are 0, so w_occ=0 and the missing reset gating cannot cause the fails.

candidates.evidence_for: Two spec statements conflict for back-to-back pointer updates. The model definition (spec:653: bits independent, 0..2 extra cycles, replacement) allows one bit of a pointer to overtake an earlier changed bit. The destination can then see a pointer value that never existed, so the occupancy estimate leaves 0..DEPTH. spec:684, REQ-FUNC-010 (spec:139) and rules.json:13573 assume the destination only ever sees the previous or current pointer, so the estimate stays within range. The RTL implements both statements literally, and the check follows the second. Fails are 0 in model_off.s1 and syn.s1 and appear in every model-on run.
candidates.evidence_against: spec:684 can be read as the intended behaviour (the destination only sees previous values). Under that reading the model, not the spec, is at fault (candidate A).

candidates.evidence_for: The model is RTL code (m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182). It makes the destination see Gray values outside the source sequence, including values ahead of the true pointer. That contradicts spec:684 and the 'never optimistic' intent of REQ-FUNC-008/009 and TEST-008 (rules.json:8782: 'flags never optimistic'). Also, o_empty=0 with w_occ 'negative' is a flag state that a coherent synchronizer cannot produce. The flag logic (rd.sv:112-118) has no protection against an incoherent synchronized pointer, but with a real synchronizer it does not need any.
candidates.evidence_against: The model follows spec:653 word for word (bits independent, replacement on change). The FIFO flag formula is exactly REQ-FUNC-010. No data or ordering error was seen (CHK-005/CHK-006: 0 fails, results.json:977-1100). Changing the flag RTL (for example, clamping w_occ) would add logic only to absorb a simulation artifact.

candidates.evidence_for: Clause (b) assumes the read-domain estimate never exceeds DEPTH, which is not true under the spec's model with back-to-back updates. The behaviour text 'and while i_rst_n_rd=0' is also unclear about the gating.
candidates.evidence_against: The contract (contract.json:287) and REQ-FUNC-010 support the clause, and rules.json:12923 says out-of-range thresholds behave deterministically. The reset gating is not the cause: w_occ=0 in reset. A test-side fix would weaken the check, which is not proposed.

analyses.options: First confirm the failing clause: add per-clause $display of i_empty_thr, o_empty, o_empty_thr and the internal w_wgray_s/reg_rbin at NNC_FAIL. The expected result is clause (b) with an incoherent w_wgray_s. Then the designer decides: (1) Clarify the spec, deciding whether the metastability model may show a pointer value outside the source sequence. If not (the intent of spec:684), (2) fix the RTL model in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv / m_vlsit_afifo_sync.sv. Options: one delay decision per synchronized vector instead of per bit, or a rule that a later bit change is not output before an earlier pending change of the same vector (keep the order). Update spec:653 to match. If yes, the spec must state the range of the estimate under the model, and REQ-FUNC-010 / CHK-003(b) / CHK-013 must say how the threshold flags behave then. That is a spec decision, not a checker edit. Also fix the CHK-003 behaviour wording ('while i_rst_n_rd=0' -> 'also while i_rst_n_rd=0') so it matches the ungated checker.

analyses.failure: CHK-013 assertion: 721 fails / 1,681,616 hits. First fail 9,712,000 ps (base.s1), during test_chk_014_nominal_latency/per=1 (14 ns write / 6 ns read; base.s1.log:40-45). Fails are 0 in model_off.s1 and syn.s1 and non-zero in every model-on run (results.json:1473-1536).
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:524: "(a) if i_full_thr==0, then o_full_thr=1; (b) if i_full_thr > PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH (9..15), then o_full_thr=0; (c) if i_full_thr==PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_full_thr == (o_full AND i_rst_n_sw AND NOT o_sw_rst_busy); (d) if o_full=1, i_rst_n_sw=1 and o_sw_rst_busy=0, then o_full_thr == (i_full_thr <= PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH)." REQ-FUNC-010 (spec:139): "o_full_thr shall be 1 when the write-domain occupancy estimate is greater than or equal to i_full_thr... a value above the depth makes it never 1". The same is in rules.json:12923. REQ-FUNC-008 (spec:137): the full flag "shall never be 0 while the FIFO is physically full". Model, spec:653: bits independent, 0..2 extra cycles, pending change replaced.
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:106: w_full_n = (reg_wgray == w_rgray_s ^ 1100). :120: w_occ = reg_wbin - gray2bin(w_rgray_s). :125-126: o_full = w_wr_blk | w_full_n; o_full_thr = w_wr_blk ? (i_full_thr==0) : (w_occ >= i_full_thr). By construction (a) and (d) hold, because a non-blocked o_full means w_occ==8. So (b)/(c) can fail only when w_occ is 9..15. Then o_full_thr=1 and o_full=0, which fails (c) with thr=8 and (b) with thr 9..w_occ. Hypothesis for the first fail: with i_full_thr=8, fill_tr drains 7 words at consecutive 6 ns read edges. The read Gray pointer changes every 6 ns while the write side samples every 14 ns. Example: rbin 6->7->8 is Gray 0101->0100->1100. If the bit0 fall gets extra delay and the bit3 rise does not, w_rgray_s=1101 = bin 9 while wbin=8. That gives w_occ=15, o_full_thr=1, o_full=0 (1100 != 0001). The read pointer seen is 9, one ahead of the true value (8), i.e. optimistic. Same root cause as CHK-003: per-bit independent delay in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182. Inferred from the code; no values are logged.
analyses.test_does: Checker nnc_chk_wr.sv:123-129, disable iff (!i_rst_n_wr), evaluated at every write edge: the four clauses as in the contract. Stimulus at the first fail: test_chk_014 per=(14,6) (test:695-707), init ft=DEPTH=8, et=0 (test:700). fill_tr fills 8 words, reads one at Tr, then reads 7 words at consecutive read edges (test:422-452, drain at :448). Later fails are in test_chk_016 pairs with random ft (test:765) and in other random tests.

candidates.evidence_for: Same conflict as CHK-003. spec:653 allows bits of one Gray pointer to be delayed independently, with replacement. spec:684, REQ-FUNC-010 ('a value above the depth makes it never 1') and rules.json:12923/13573 assume the synchronized pointer is always a past value. The RTL follows the formula, and the check follows the range assumption. Fails are 0 with model off / syn and appear in all model-on runs, including chk_014 per=1, where the read pointer changes faster than the write clock samples.
candidates.evidence_against: spec:684 and REQ-FUNC-008 ('never optimistic') can be read as binding on the model, which would make this an RTL-model defect (A).

candidates.evidence_for: The RTL model (m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182) can present w_rgray_s = a read pointer value ahead of the true one (e.g. 9 when only 8 reads happened). That is an optimistic synchronized pointer, against REQ-FUNC-008 and TEST-008 (rules.json:8782 'flags never optimistic'). In a full FIFO, the same reordering could make o_full=0 while physically full. Example: wbin=0 (wrapped) with true rbin=8 and seen rbin_s=9 gives w_full_n=0. That would allow an overwrite of unread data.
candidates.evidence_against: The model is exactly as spec:653 describes. The FIFO flag RTL (wr.sv:106-126) is the specified formula and is correct for any coherent synchronizer: syn.s1 and model_off.s1 have 0 fails. CHK-006 (never optimistic against the true occupancy) has 0 fails in all 14 runs, so no unsafe flag was observed.

candidates.evidence_for: Clauses (b)/(c) assume the write-domain estimate is at most DEPTH, which the spec's per-bit model does not guarantee.
candidates.evidence_against: The contract (contract.json:524) and the spec answers (rules.json:12923) state the range behaviour explicitly. The checker matches the contract clause by clause (nnc_chk_wr.sv:124-129). Changing it would weaken the check.

analyses.options: First, log at each CHK-013 fail: i_full_thr, o_full, o_full_thr, and the internal reg_wbin and w_rgray_s (u_wr). That confirms w_occ>8 from an incoherent w_rgray_s, and which clause fails. Then the same decision as CHK-003 applies, and one fix should cover both. (1) Clarify the spec on whether the metastability model may show a synchronized pointer value outside the source sequence, given REQ-FUNC-008 'never optimistic' and REQ-FUNC-010 'above the depth never 1'. (2) If not allowed, fix the RTL simulation model (m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv / m_vlsit_afifo_sync.sv) to keep the vector coherent: one delay per vector, or keep the order of pending bit changes. Update spec:653. (3) If allowed, the spec must define o_full_thr for an estimate above DEPTH. A saturating compare in wr.sv:120-126 is possible, but it only hides a simulation artifact and would mask a real optimistic-pointer problem. In that case, also check whether o_full can be 0 while physically full, using a directed full-FIFO plus fast-read stimulus.
